questions.q: Given that $\mathrm{y}=(\sin x)^x \cdot x^{\sin x}+\mathrm{a}^x$, find $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}$.
questions.solution:
As, $y=(\sin x)^x \cdot x^{\sin x}+a^x=u+a^x \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d u}{d x}+\frac{d\left(a^x\right)}{d x}$
where $u=(\sin x)^x . x^{\sin x} \Rightarrow \log u=x \log (\sin x)+\sin x . \log x$ on differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get
$\Rightarrow \frac{d u}{d x}=(\sin x)^x \cdot x^{\sin x}\left[\log (\sin x)+x \cot x+\frac{\sin x}{x}+\log x \cdot \cos x\right]$
Thus, $\frac{d y}{d x}=(\sin x)^x \cdot x^{\sin x}\left[\log (\sin x)+x \cot x+\frac{\sin x}{x}+\log x \cdot \cos x\right]+a^x \log a$

questions.q: If $y=e^{x^2 \cos x}+(\cos x)^x$, then find $\frac{d y}{d x}$.
questions.solution:
Let $\mathrm{u}=(\cos \mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}^2 \cdot \cos \mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{u}$
$\therefore \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}^2 \cdot \cos \mathrm{x}}\left(2 \mathrm{x} \cdot \cos \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{x}^2 \cdot \sin \mathrm{x}\right)+\frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dx}}$
$\log \mathrm{u}=\log (\cos \mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \log \mathrm{u}=\mathrm{x} \cdot \log (\cos \mathrm{x})$
Differentiate w.r.t. "x"
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}} \frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\log (\cos \mathrm{x})-\mathrm{x} \tan \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dx}}=(\cos \mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{x}}\{\log (\cos x)-x \tan x\}$
Therefore,
$\frac{d y}{d x}=e^{x^2 \cdot \cos x}\left(2 x \cdot \cos x-x^2 \cdot \sin x\right)+(\cos x)^x\{\log (\cos x)-x \tan x\}$

questions.q: If $x \sqrt{1+y}+y \sqrt{1+x}=0$ and $x \neq y$, prove that $\frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{1}{(x+1)^2}$.
questions.solution:
$x \sqrt{1+y}+y \sqrt{1+x}=0 \Rightarrow x \sqrt{1+y}=-y \sqrt{1+x}$
Squaring to get: $x^2(1+y)=y^2(1+x)$
Simplifying to get: $(x-y)(x+y+x y)=0$
$\text { As, } x
eq y \quad \therefore y=-\frac{x}{1+x}$
Differentiating w.r.t. ' x ', we get:
$\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{-1(1+x)-(-x) \cdot 1}{(1+x)^2}=\frac{-1}{(1+x)^2}$
